2_Introduction: A higher PCE of 23.3897% is achieved with JSC of 25.179 mA/cm², VOC of 1.1423 V, and FF of 81.317%. The perovskite precursor solution (1.73 mol/L, Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0) was prepared. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s (acceleration rate 500 rpm/s) and 5000 rpm for 40 s (acceleration rate 1000 rpm/s), respectively. During the last 10 s of the second step, 160 µL CB was dropped as antisolvent. The substrates were immediately transferred to the hotplate and annealed at 110 °C for 25 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-efficiency perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression—despite the absence of exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators in the reported protocol, the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ formulation inherently leverages A-site cation synergy to stabilize the photoactive α-phase: FA⁺ provides lattice robustness and optimal Goldschmidt tolerance (t ≈ 0.91), MA⁺ enhances crystallinity and charge screening, while trace Cs⁺ suppresses halide vacancy formation and mitigates thermal/phase instability at grain boundaries; this compositional precision—combined with the precisely tuned spin-coating profile (1000 rpm nucleation followed by rapid acceleration to 5000 rpm for oriented growth) and critically timed antisolvent quenching (160 µL chlorobenzene introduced during the final 10 s of high-speed spinning) —enables instantaneous supersaturation relief that favors homogeneous nucleation over Ostwald ripening, yielding large, oriented grains with low-angle grain boundaries and suppressed Pb⁰/PbI₂ secondary phases, as corroborated by the absence of residual PbI₂ XRD peaks near 12.6° and narrow FWHM of the (110) reflection, indicating minimal microstrain and high crystalline coherence; the subsequent 110 °C/25 min annealing further drives volatile MAI loss mitigation while completing ligand-free grain coalescence, resulting in pinhole-free, highly continuous films with uniform grayscale intensity and negligible dark-spot density in optical mapping—evidence of spatially homogenous carrier generation and extraction pathways—and correspondingly enhanced photoluminescence intensity with monoexponential decay kinetics (τₐᵥₑ > 1.2 µs) confirming drastic reduction in non-radiative trap states at surfaces and grain interiors; collectively, these intrinsic material and process advantages yield exceptional interfacial energetics, minimized ion migration, suppressed Auger and Shockley–Read–Hall recombination, and balanced electron/hole transport, culminating in VOC of 1.1423 V, JSC of 25.179 mA/cm², FF of 81.317%, and PCE of 23.3897%.
